fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on change-set-records-dispatch): The leaf has a change set 'record its kind' (feature, bug, milestone) and its acceptance checks 'kind bug' and 'kind feature' in change show --json. But a change set already has a kind with another meaning: changeset.Kind is intention or record (internal/changeset/body.go:66-77), `rhiza change new --kind` takes intention|record (internal/api/change.go:63), and change show --json already prints "kind": "intention"/"record". As written, the new field collides with or overwrites the existing one, and a milestone request's change set would need kind both 'record' and 'milestone'. The leaf (and decision workflow-dispatch-rules-file, 'rhiza change show shows the change set's recorded kind') should name a distinct field, e.g. request_kind, in the open entry and in change show. The critic confirmed it: A change set already has a kind with another meaning: changeset.Kind is intention|record (internal/changeset/body.go:66-77), change new --kind takes intention|record (internal/api/change.go:63) and change show --json prints "kind" from c.Open.Kind (change.go:220,304). change-set-records-dispatch says the change set 'records its kind' and its acceptance reads 'kind bug'/'kind feature' in change show --json, so the new field collides with the existing one (a milestone request's change set is kind record). The leaf and decision workflow-dispatch-rules-file need a distinct field name. How should it be settled?
